name: Barrett Plastics
old_description: Barrett Plastics, LLC. is a plastic injection molding company located in northwest Arkansas, USA, where we specialize in both proprietary and custom molding.
about:
Barrett Plastics, LLC operates from Harrison, Arkansas, in the northwest corner of the state. The company was founded in 2024 and focuses on plastic injection molding, offering both proprietary and custom molding services. Ownership details and founder names have not been disclosed publicly.

Its production floor houses injection molding machines ranging from 101 to 528 tons, supported by an in-house design, fabrication, and mold shop that includes a vertical CNC milling center and modern diagnostic equipment. The company maintains an on-site warehouse and a separate off-site facility to enable just-in-time delivery of finished goods. Standard product lines include a variety of caps — such as fez, stand-up, flat, snap-on, lube, reverse-taper, flat-top piercer, and grease-tip styles — as well as cartridge plungers. Quality management is certified to ISO 9001.

The company serves customers requiring custom injection-molded components, though specific industry sectors are not detailed in its public materials.

Barrett Plastics emphasizes precision and quality, noting continuous improvement in business practices and processes to expand its customer base.

name: Barth Electronics
old_description: Please contact Barth Electronics, Inc. for general company inquiries and technical information on Pulse Power products or ESD test equipment. Complete our contact form with your information, requests and feedback.
about:
Barth Electronics, Inc. has been headquartered in Boulder City, Nevada since 1976, when the company relocated from Ohio to support weapons testing at the Nevada Test Site. Founded in 1964, the firm began by designing and manufacturing specialized test hardware for EG&G in Las Vegas and for national laboratories.

The company designs and manufactures sub-nanosecond high-energy pulse power instrumentation, including over 100 distinct pulse power products. In 1997 its engineers developed the first commercial Transmission Line Pulser (TLP) for the electrostatic discharge (ESD) industry. Today the product line encompasses the Model 4002 TLP+ for human-body-model testing, the Model 4012 VFTLP+ for charged-device-model testing, the Model 4702 HMM+ for IEC-equivalent gun discharge testing, and a 700-series of 3 kV and 5 kV pulse generators. All ESD testing services are performed in-house at the Boulder City factory, and a rental program is offered for the Model 4002 TLP+.

Barth serves the semiconductor industry with ESD device characterization and qualification testing, while its pulse power instruments are used daily in physics and pulse-power laboratories worldwide. Historical customers include EG&G and U.S. national laboratories involved in weapons testing.

The company traces its high-reliability standards to its weapons-testing heritage: “By beating our swords into plowshares, weapons testing hardware was changed into the development and manufacture of the highest quality ESD test equipment available today.” It continues to investigate new technologies for ESD and high-voltage pulse power as needs emerge.

name: Base Power Company
old_description: Base Power is an Austin, Texas-based company that designs, assembles, and deploys home battery backup systems while operating as a retail electric provider in Texas.
about:
Base Power Company was founded in 2023 in Austin, Texas, by CEO Zach Dell and co-founder Justin Lopas. Lopas previously led manufacturing at Anduril and worked on rockets at SpaceX, while the broader team brings experience from satellite constellation launches and early electric vehicle production. The company was born after Winter Storm Uri left millions of Texans without power for days, highlighting the grid’s fragility and rising electricity costs.

Base designs, assembles, and deploys its Core home battery backup system — a 39.2 kWh unit that provides 36 to 72 hours of whole-home backup — and operates as a retail electric provider in Texas and Illinois. The company handles battery pack assembly, in-house engineering, UL-certified testing, and runs a virtual power plant that dispatches stored energy to the grid during peak demand.

The primary customers are residential homeowners in Texas and Illinois seeking affordable backup power and fixed-rate electricity. The company also serves grid-storage and utility markets by aggregating its distributed batteries to provide grid-balancing services. Testimonials cite installations in Houston, Waxahachie, Cypress, Arlington, Saginaw, and Pflugerville.

Base positions its model as a low-cost alternative to traditional generators or solar-plus-storage, installing the battery for a $695 one-time fee plus a $19 monthly membership, with an all-in energy rate around 13.9¢/kWh. The battery is tested for -22°F to 122°F and submersion-rated to three feet, and the company says it earns revenue from grid services rather than marking up energy, allowing it to keep rates low.

name: Basic American Foods
old_description: Jack Hume founded Basic American Foods in 1933 with the belief that integrity and taste were paramount, and it’s these same beliefs that drive us today. While we started as a modest dehydration plant in California, we’ve grown our company and our capabilities over the last 85 years becoming the market leader, because we want to help people serve great food to as many people as possible. That’s why you’ll find our foods and brands in restaurants, schools, hospitals, grocery, and club stores around the world.
about:
Basic American Foods was founded in 1933 by Jack Hume as a modest dehydration plant in California. The company is now headquartered in Idaho Falls, Idaho, and maintains an additional office in Walnut Creek, California.

The company manufactures a range of food products, leveraging dehydration and other food processing capabilities developed over decades. It has grown to become a market leader in its category, supplying products designed to be delicious, easy to prepare, and accessible.

Basic American Foods sells its products through multiple channels: restaurants, schools, hospitals, grocery stores, and club stores worldwide. Its customer base spans foodservice operators, institutional kitchens, and retail outlets.

The founder's original belief that integrity and taste are paramount continues to drive the business. The company states its mission is to make real food heroes every day by providing foods that are delicious to eat, easy to prepare, and accessible to all.

about:
Battlefield Fabrication operates from Searcy, Arkansas, serving White County and the surrounding Central Arkansas region. The company is a small, family-owned business that describes itself as a licensed and insured contractor specializing in metal-roofed buildings and portable structures. No founding year or founder names are disclosed in public materials.

Its core services span the full build cycle: site preparation and dirt work including clearing and grading; concrete foundations such as slabs and footings; custom construction of barndominiums, pole barns, stud‑wall shops, and portable buildings; and metal roofing installation using standing‑seam or exposed‑fastener systems. The firm also supplies building kits for shops and portable structures, along with hardware, fasteners, luxury vinyl plank flooring, and counter tops. No facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures are published.

Customers include homeowners, agricultural operators, and commercial clients seeking turnkey buildings for residential, farm, or light‑industrial use. Concrete examples from the company’s own descriptions include barndominiums for living space, pole barns for equipment storage, custom shops for workshops, and portable buildings for flexible occupancy. The business focuses on the White County area but notes a broader Central Arkansas reach.

Battlefield Fabrication emphasizes seamless communication from start to finish, affordable pricing on quality metal‑roofed buildings, and a single‑source approach that handles dirt work, concrete, framing, and roofing under one contract. The company also highlights warranties on its metal roofing installations as a differentiator.

about:
Baycable operates from Fremont, California, where it has been building custom cable assemblies and interconnect solutions for over five decades. The company marks its 50th year in business, though a specific founding year is not published. Ownership structure and founder names have not been disclosed publicly.

The company designs and manufactures electro-mechanical assemblies, molded cable assemblies, coil cords, and custom cable products. Production spans two ISO-registered facilities in North America and includes an in-house machine shop that produces mold tools and custom components. Baycable supports prototype through medium-volume runs and maintains certified in-house IPC-620 trainers. Its engineering team comprises compound, process, and electronic engineers who provide comprehensive design support.

Baycable serves OEMs, ODMs, and their contractors across medical, industrial, automotive, audio, and semiconductor markets. Concrete examples from its portfolio include medical RF generator cables and automotive defrost coil assemblies. The company emphasizes application-specific solutions for complex interconnection challenges.

Baycable states its mission is driven by a commitment to excellence, quality, reliability, and ingenuity. It differentiates itself through unparalleled customer service, comprehensive design support, and innovative solutions that enable customer success, aiming to engineer connections that drive progress across every industry it serves.

name: Bayou Solar LLC
old_description: Our major suppliers are leading providers of solar energy technology, offering low-maintenance, fully integrated high-performance systems engineered for efficiency and long life, and designed to fit your lifestyle.
about:
Bayou Solar LLC was founded in 2007 in Elmwood, Louisiana, a suburb of New Orleans. The company operates as a Louisiana state‑licensed contractor with a specialty in solar energy equipment, providing turnkey solar installations for residential customers. No founder names or ownership structure are disclosed in public records.

The firm designs and installs fully integrated solar power systems sourced from major suppliers of photovoltaic and thermal technology. Its service includes a free on‑site evaluation by a solar consultant, who assesses a home’s hot‑water heater type (gas, electric, or propane) and pool heating needs to size the system. Bayou Solar does not manufacture its own panels or inverters; it acts as an installer and integrator, delivering low‑maintenance, high‑performance arrays engineered for efficiency and long life.

The primary market is homeowners in the Greater New Orleans area seeking to reduce energy costs through renewable energy. The company highlights the 30 % federal tax credit as a key incentive for clients. Its project scope covers both solar electric and solar thermal applications, including pool heating, positioning it within the renewable energy and solar equipment sectors.

Bayou Solar emphasizes that its systems are built from leading‑supplier technology and are tailored to each household’s lifestyle, a differentiator it traces to its founding goal of making solar practical for everyday Louisiana residents.

about:
Becker Electronics, Inc. has operated from Ronkonkoma, New York, since its founding in 1996. The company began as a custom electronics manufacturer and expanded steadily by emphasizing customer service, quality control, and flexibility in a changing market.

The shop specializes in build-to-print contract manufacturing, producing custom cable assemblies, wire harnesses, mechanical assemblies, and panel and box builds. Its capabilities include intricate soldering, multiconductor and flat-ribbon cable assembly, complex wire harness fabrication, and wire preparation. The facility runs on high-speed production equipment and maintains a large inventory supported by international sourcing channels.

Becker serves customers in automated lighting, military, communication systems, audio, home automation, and solar industries. The company also partners with D2P, a design-to-production platform, to extend its service reach.

Leadership attributes the company’s growth to a devotion to satisfying customer needs, with a stated policy that the answer to client requests is “yes.” The operation holds AS9100:2016 certification, reflecting its quality management commitment for aerospace and defense work.

Beer City Metal Works differentiates itself by prioritizing communication as a core project requirement and by offering design support that bridges napkin sketches to production-ready models. This approach aims to reduce misunderstandings and streamline the path from idea to installed metalwork.
